explanation: The characteristic polynomial is det(A−λI)=(1−λ)(λ²+λ−2)=−(λ−1)²(λ+2). Thus the eigenvalues are 1 (multiplicity 2) and −2. The nonzero rows of A−I are (5,−4,−1) and its negative, so rank(A−I)=1 and the eigenspace for 1 has dimension 2. Together with the one-dimensional eigenspace for −2, this gives three independent eigenvectors. Therefore A is diagonalizable with D=diag(1,1,−2).
